Dia desses a nossa pauta do Despertador foi sobre finanças. Eu sempre tive dificuldades em guardar dinheiro. 

Há exatos 5 anos eu realizei um dos grandes sonhos da minha vida. Conheci NY. Para isso, guardei dois anos de cachê em sales. O sale era uma ação de venda que rolava na rádio aos sábados de manhã (eu sempre disse que precisava de uma voz no sábado pela manhã… ???).

Planejar aquela viagem fez eu criar um novo relacionamento com as minhas finanças. Essa viagem, definitivamente, mudou a minha vida. 

Sobre NY, eu fiquei tão impactado, que acho que nem aproveitei como deveria. Me emocionei em várias quadras, parques e prédios. Era como se a Sessão da Tarde fosse algo real e eu estava fazendo parte daquilo.

Sonho todos os dias em voltar a NY. Nem que seja para fingir costume. ?

We forget. Don’t we?

We forget that things don’t have to be difficult. We make things so much harder than we think that they should be.

For the longest time I HATED unloading the dishwasher (now, I wish I had one! ?)

I thought that it was going to take SO MUCH TIME - at least it SEEMED that it would take at LEAST 1/2 an hour! And I just didn’t have that much time to dedicate to unloading it.

Unloading the dishwasher, in my mind, was difficult and time consuming.

Until I timed myself.

Seriously. I actually got out my phone, started the timer, and timed how long it actually took me to unload the dishwasher.

Want to know how long it took me to unload it?

5 MINUTES!

It totally changed my attitude about unloading the dishwasher. After that, I still didn’t love it, but it wasn’t as big of a struggle to do it.

The same thing is true with your health habits.

The obstacles that we create in our heads are SO MUCH BIGGER than they are in real life.

Helping others become the best versions of themselves and unlock the person they know they’re capable of being is what I’m passionate about, I want to be the person I was so fortunate to find!

شیر ایرانی(شیر آسیایی) 
Panthera leo persicus
عکاسی شده در هند؛
‌❤این سری عکس ها برای سی امین سال عکاسی من از حیات وحش تقدیم میشود.❤
این عکس از شیر ایرانی یا آسیایی را در تنها زیستگاه باقی مانده این گربه سان،یعنی هند گرفتم.
سال هشتاد و هشت برای دیدنش به هند سفر کردم و هزار بار افسوس خوردم که چرا لیاقت داشتنش را نداشتیم.زیستگاهش را نابود کردیم و طعمه هایش را منقرض.
این گونه روزگاری از شمال یونان و ترکیه تا خاورمیانه و هند پراکندگی داشت.
ولی امروز تنها تعداد کمی در هند باقی مانده.
زیستگاهش که زمانی از دشت ارژن شیراز تا خوزستان و بوشهر بود،تبدیل به روستا و زمین کشاورزی شده و گوزن زرد که اصلی ترین غذای او بوده، در آن منطقه منقرض.
جثه شیر ایرانی از شیر آفریقایی کوچکتر و یالش کم پشت تر و پوست آویزانی در زیر بدن دیده میشود.
شیر همواره در ایران نماد قدرت بود و از زمان ساسانیان بر پرچم ایران حضور داشت.
چه آسان به دست بی رحم انقراض سپردیمش.
کاش به فکر یوز و پلنگ و باقیمانده نحیف و شکننده حیات وحش وطنمان باشیم.

Why do I always talk about a balanced lifestyle and a sustainable approach to your goals?⬇️

The truth is because as a young teen I really didn’t understand what that meant. I grew up in the era where skinny and detox teas were cool, where eating carbs made you ‘fat’ and eating ‘clean’ and cutting out my fav foods was essential for fat loss☹️

Only to find out that I was actually doing more harm to my body physically and mentally than I was good ?

When I took it upon myself to learn about a balanced lifestyle I started to enjoy social occasions, eating the food I wanted to eat in moderation and working hard in the gym consistently..it actually amazed me how much growth I saw mentally and physically but also the results were far greater ✨

To succeed at your goals you need to make them realistic & make them to fit into your lifestyle, not the other way around ?

It absolutely possible to find balance in your life and reach your desired outcome! Please don’t let anyone tell you otherwis

She had it all - Money, Fame, Success. But then stomach cancer put her on her death bed. World-renowned fashion designer and author Kyrzayda “Crisda” Rodriguez wrote this before she died at age 40:

1. I had the world's most expensive car in my garage but now I have to move in a wheelchair.

2. My house sells all kinds of branded clothes, shoes and valuables, but now my body is wrapped in a small cloth provided by the hospital.

3. I have plenty of money in the bank. But now I benefit nothing from this amount.

4. My house was like a castle but now I'm sleeping on two beds in the hospital.

5. From five star hotel to five star hotel. But right now I'm spending time in the hospital moving from lab to lab

6. I have given hundreds of people signatures but this time medical records are my signature.

7. I've had seven barbers to do my hair, but now - I don't have a hair on my head.

8. Traveled in a private jet, I can fly anywhere, but now I need two aids to walk to the hospital door.

9.

Bicep Training ?

Growing big biceps comes down to a few key principles and movements. Here's an overview of how to do so!

Compound Movement: Chin Ups show good activation of the biceps and are great for the lower end of the rep range spectrum to expose your biceps to heavy weight. Also, underhand barbell rows can be good for this as well.

Isolation Movements: The classic barbell curl is a staple in building big biceps. If I had to pick one movement for the biceps, it would be the barbell curl everytime hands down.
Other good exercises include the hammer grip cable curl and the dumbbell curl. Each expose the muscle to a bit of variation and hit the muscle in a slightly different way creating well rounded biceps.

posts.caption_text: Finally getting around to this mobility challenge ?‍♀️

// abdominals //

When you @pilates.with.ivana says August is for ab workouts, you kind of run with it…❤️‍?

Playing around with:
Reverse crunches
Roll overs
Control balance
Leg changes

@seanbergarapilates and I played around with these last summer (he probably had this set up in his pockets for a lot longer though ?). I wasn’t able to get my set up to work and so I never shared. Finally found a way (hello foot-strap)?

Be sure to co-contract your core as you lower the legs to the carriage to protect the low back (it feels like forever finding that footing!).

Also a special shout out to @zaynagold @judytamspilates with their #pilatesismagic August theme: Age Defying. When I do moves like this at 54 I do feel like I’m defying the concept of what aging means. But I’m also able to do moves like this because of a commitment I made to my mental and physical health for my overall well-being long ago. It’s never too late to start that journey! That’s the real age defying process ?

いきまっし金沢

#金沢 #卯辰山 #東茶屋街 

久しぶりに金沢を朝ラン。

These are my top four favorite snatches, in order. 

Full snatches didn't even make the list, and they were left out on purpose. Controversially, I think they're annoying.

Here's my hot take: I don't enjoy callusing my hands, and reps upon reps of full snatches will more easily tear your skin than will half snatches. 

The steelman argument in favor of the full snatch: you gain more strength by controlling the greater elastic eccentric energy caused by the overhead bell drop.

While this is probably true on a per-rep basis, the rep counts inevitably decrease over time because full snatches absolutely tear skin quicker than half snatches. And if you can do twice or even three times more volume with half snatches than with full, I imagine the potential strength gain differential becomes nullified and even reversed over time. 

On top of that, half snatches feel more controlled to me. 

At the end of the day, I enjoy half snatches more. And because I enjoy them, I do them more often. And

24 min emom (every minute on the minute):
MIN 1: 20 deficit push ups
MIN 2: 20 sit ups
MIN 3: 15 burpees
MIN 4: 20 goblet squats (15kg/35lb)
⠀⠀⠀⠀
Workout flow: you have one minute to complete the prescribed reps set out in each minute. Whatever time is left over  is yours to rest before moving onto the next minutes work. Continue moving through this format for the full 24 minutes.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
Workout notes: the first two rounds are fairly straightforward, I started to feel the push ups in the third round and everything gets real spicy in rounds five & six ?
Break the push ups up if you need to. I did sets of 5 in the fourth round onwards. Try to complete everything with 50 seconds, some rest is better than none! Scale back the reps if you’re struggling to complete the set number within the minute.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
Scaling:
• reduce reps/time of emom
• knees down deficit push ups
• crunches for sit ups
• half burpees/down ups
• reduce weight of db/squat jumps/air squats

Aprende a hacer THE PULL OVER en 3 pasos ?

0️⃣ Disfruta del proceso

1️⃣ Trabaja tus pull up estrictas: Es el primer paso para conseguir tus Pull over pero además os vendrá genial para el resto de movimientos gimnasticos.

2️⃣ Toes to bar: Haremos una versión diferente del toes to bar con las piernas flexionadas. Mete las rodillas entre los brazos y la barra para tener un poco más de giro de lo normal. Cuando consigas este paso, añade una flexión de brazos antes de llevar las rodillas a la barra. Si consigues este último paso ya casi lo tienes.

3️⃣ Trabaja en barra baja o en barra alta con ayuda del un cajón: Empieza subiendo primero una pierna para tener más velocidad en la subida y que sea más fácil. Así poco a poco te acostumbrarás a dar la vuelta que a veces da miedo.  Después añádele más dificultad haciéndolo con los pies juntos. 

Si completas los niveles anteriores estarás preparad@ para intentarlo de forma completa en la posición de colgado.

?Eu sou especialista em treinamento com peso corporal e Metcon,(Cross Training). Para trazer para VOCÊ credibilidade e mais opções, para melhorar em seus resultados.

?Condicionamento metabólico ou “metcon” para abreviar é um estilo de treinamento popularizado nos últimos anos pela Cross Training – embora o estilo de treinamento em si não seja novo. O termo descreve períodos curtos de treinamento de alta intensidade projetados para aumentar a demanda metabólica e aumentar o uso de energia.

?O metcon segue um formato de métodos HIIT (treinamento intervalado de alta intensidade), For time, amrap emom e dentre outros. Sugerido o mais rápido possível de acordo com o nível de condicionamento de cada um.

L’ONDA DI ROCCIA

Wave Rock, nota anche come Katter Kich dai Noongar, un popolo di indigeni australiani, è una formazione rocciosa naturale che ha la forma di un’alta onda oceanica che si sta per “schiantare”. 

L’”onda” è alta circa 15 metri e lunga circa 110 metri, e forma il lato nord di una collina solitaria, conosciuta come “Hyden Rock”. 

Questa collina, formata da granito, si trova a circa 3 chilometri a est della piccola città di Hyden e a 296 chilometri a est-sudest di Perth, nell’Australia occidentale. 

Wave Rock e Hyden Rock fanno parte della riserva naturale di Hyden Wildlife Park, grande 160 ettari, che viene visitata da oltre 100.00 turisti all’anno.

Segui @different_group se sei appassionato di scienza e divulgazione.

Fonte: Kaartdijin Noongar, Central Wheatbelt Visitor Centre

Mobility ? let’s put some attention to the mobility of our joints and moving through our active range of motion. Good mobility means that the range of motion is relatively smooth, more resilient against injury, helps maintain a healthy body and better able to recruit the most muscle mass for each exercise. 

I personally like incorporating mobility focused drills or exercises as part of my routine to work on refining movement patterns as well. When we run, walk, lift, we typically are doing the same movements over & over again, so making sure our body is mobile & happy is key for performance. I haven’t been incorporating it as much lately so this little mobility moves session was needed ?

FULL BODY METCON !!! 

Metcon training is a type of workout that most commonly combines strength and cardio conditioning, as well as both anaerobic and aerobic exercises. 

It’s one of my favourite type of training methods as it allows to you build good muscles mass while improving your cardiovascular fitness. 

Energy systems used : 

Aerobic fitness - to complete the entire workout 
Lactic acid system - to complete the anaerobic exercises 
Creatine phosphate - to complete the strength exercises 

I paired a plyometric movements with a strength movement in an antagonist format ( working opposing muscle groups ) 

The workout : 

20 Kettlebell swings 
10 Dumbbell bench press 
8 Kettlbell Pendlay Rows
10 Alt arm devil press 
15 cal row 
20 kettlbell deadlifts 
8 Barbell snatch 
24 Butterfly crunches 

60 mins on the clock complete as many rounds as possible 

I got 8 rounds !
